messages.subject: Re: Error message "No rows to aggregate"
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Joerg,

I just saw your post over on the Skyline support board, where you mentioned that you were using small molecules.
MSstats does not work with small molecules. The reason for this is that the MSstats Input report relies on the "PeptideModifiedSequence" column which is blank for small molecules.
I am not sure whether any sort of workaround exists for this, or whether there are plans to support small molecules in the future.

messages.body_plain: The documentation states "The recommended format includes Acquired Time, Peptide name, Annotations and data for any QC metrics such as Retention Time, Total Peak Area and Mass Accuracy etc." What other features of the data can MSstatsQC utilise that are referred to by "etc."? This format is described as "recommended", so what are the necessary columns and other optional columns which can be provided to calculate more metrics? Are there plans to make it more generally applicable to other kinds of proteomics, such as SWATH-MS data, by allowing more input data formats, such as output files created by OpenSWATH?

messages.subject: Re: Clearer Specification of MSstatsQC Input File Format
messages.subject_clean: Clearer Specification of MSstatsQC Input File Format
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dario,

Thanks for following up. MSstatsQC input format requires Acquired Time, Peptide name, and Annotations columns as three necessary input columns. After Annotations,you can parse any metric of interest depending on the workflow you obtain QC data. Retention time, peak area and mass accuracy are just examples generated from Skyline output. MSstatsQC focuses on data analysis rather than calculating metrics.

We are currently expanding MSstatsQC for DDA outputs and SWATH-MS is another possible direction. Please let me know if there is any available QC outputs generated from OpenSWATH. I would like to test to see what to fix for better results.

Thanks,
Eralp

I'll appreciate suggestions on how to resolve this error.

messages.subject: Re: error when use with Skyline for absolute quant
messages.subject_clean: error when use with Skyline for absolute quant
messages.body_plain:
The problem is that you have several replicates that come from the same .wiff file. I guess MSstats does not work with these multi-sample wiff files.

One way to work around this problem would be to change the MSstats Input so that it uses the full path to the file (including the WIFF sample name), instead of just the bare filename.

I have attached a file "DifferentMSstatsInput.skyr" which does this.

The way that you use that .skyr file to replace the MSstats input that the MSstats external tool uses, is to do the following in Skyline:
File > Export > Report
Click the "Edit List" button
In the "Group" dropdown at the top, choose "External Tools"
Click the "Import" button
Choose the file "DifferentMSstatsInput.skyr" that I have attache to this message.
Skyline will ask you if you want to replace the existing "MSstats Input". Say "yes".

After this, the MSstats external tool should work for you, and not give you any errors about duplicate rows.

messages.subject: MSstatsTMT Feedback and Questions
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I enjoyed learning about the newest addition to the MSstats family, MSstatsTMT, at US HUPO. I have downloaded the latest package from GitHub (0.3.3) and started to test it out on my TMT data. I have processed a test dataset successfully through the functions, but have a few questions and comments.

1) In the PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat function, when I set the which.proteinid argument = "Master.Protein.Accessions", I get a data frame error.  If I use "Protein.Accessions", it completes successfully. I verified my input data contains the "Master.Protein.Accessions" column.  When I looked at the R code, I think there could be a command missing in Section 3 "get subset columns" that whould rename the "Master.Protein.Accessions" column to "ProteinName".

2) User specified pairwise comparisons: In the groupComparison.TMT function, I would like to specify specific pairwise comparisons and in a specific ratio, e.g. 'Treatment/Control' not 'Control/Treatment'. I see the documentation should allow for this, and that I should provide a matrix so that only specific pairwise comparisons are performed,  but I can't figure out how to define the contrast.matrix argument. If you can provide extra guidance on this point, and perhaps an example syntax, that would be great!

3) Is it correct that package provides normalization between different TMT mixtures (between MS runs), but not within mixes (between channels)? In my dataset (and perhaps many TMT datasets),  there are technical errors introduced during sample processing (e.g., determining protein/peptide concentrations, enzyme digestion, mixing of TMT-labeled peptides). From my use of the package it doesn't appear that the intensities within the same TMT Mixture are being normalized? Could the Central Limit Theorem or a similar concept be invoked here to correct for these errors?
Also, with respect to normalization between MS runs, I see that the user can annotate specific channel(s) as "Norm".  This use of a reference channel is useful, but not all of our experiments allow for a pooled reference channel.  It would be great to have an alternative "between MS run" normalization strategy that does not depend on a pooled reference.

Thanks in advance for your help and for creating a great TMT analysis package!

Best,
Todd

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT Feedback and Questions
messages.body_plain:
Hi Todd,

Thank you for trying MSstatsTMT and all the valuable comments. They are very helpful.

For your questions,
(1) the bug has already fixed in the new update of MSstatsTMT. You can download the package again and try it.
(2) I have added two examples of using contrast.matrix to the manual and the vignettes. The examples show how to specify one or two pairwise comparisons
(3) You are right. MSstatsTMT provides the masterpool-based normalization between TMT runs, not between channels. So currently the package only supports between-runs normalization based on reference channels. We will consider the case that reference channel is not available in our future work. The normalization between channels within each run is still under discussion. We need to further evaluate how much it can help for pairwise comparison.

Best,
Ting

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT Feedback and Questions
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ting,

Thank you for the quick reply.  The updated package resolved the error I was getting with Master.Protein.Accessions argument. The example contrast matrix was very helpful.

I had one addition question/comment regarding the handling of PSM summarization across fractions from the same mixture, specifically the fraction = TRUE argument in the PDtoMSstats converter. My dataset has 13 fractions for each mixture. When I set fraction = TRUE, then any feature found in > 1 fraction is removed and that quantified peptide is lost.  In general for most proteomic experiments, when biochemical peptide fractionation is performed, I think it is relatively common to have a significant number of peptides in > 1 fraction. So setting the fraction = TRUE argument reduced my number of quantified peptides significantly. If I set the argument to FALSE and retain these peptides, then at the protein.summarization step, the protein will have separate quantification for each fraction number. This doesn't seem to be a desired outcome, so my conclusion is if the experiment has fractions, then this argument should be set to TRUE.

So I'm wondering if it is possible when fractions = TRUE, to perform an additional summarization of PSM quantification across fractions using the same or similar function as used per run, i.e. max or sum in summaryforMultipleRows?

Best,
Todd
